main_body: A square hay bale drawn as a flat panel seen from the front, with a vertical dark brown strap down the middle and a horizontal seam at about row 8. The two halves are straw-coloured with sparse darker dots.
top_band: none. Rows 3-7 are light straw (#d4b05c), but the same tone and texture continue below the seam at row 8 as mid straw (#bc9844/#a88436). The seam is a single 1-row line, so there is no distinct top surface.
evidence: The scan at x=8 shows an outline at row 2, light straw at rows 3-7, one darker line at row 8, then alternating mid straw at rows 9-13 and an outline at row 14. The row 8 line is a 1px seam, not a front-edge highlight, and no eave shadow sits under it. The step from L=177 to L=153 is about 24, below the 25 threshold, so the upper region is the same face as the lower. The strap and the cross seam read as binding lines on one flat face, like a window with a mullion. No horizontal surface is seen from above, so this is a front elevation, not a 3/4 box.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 17-20 per tile and 38-40 colours in the references. Its main straw ramp has about 3 steps (light, mid, dark). The outline is a tinted dark brown and not neutral, which is good, and there are no 5x5 flat fills thanks to scattered dots and rows of alternating tone. The texture is sparse and regular, and the shading is much shallower than the references, so it would look thinner next to them.
